official.deadline_note: First-year domestic applicants choose Early Action I (November 1), Early Action II (January 31) or Regular Decision (March 31), with a May 1 reply deadline; international applicants have a single November 30 deadline and are notified by March 31. No extensions are granted.

Show strong academic accomplishments; Berea is academically competitive with an average ACT of about 25 and more than half of first-year students in the top fifth of their high school class
All applicants must submit a FAFSA (2027-2028 FAFSA, Berea code 001955) to be considered for admission, and refile every year enrolled

official.application_route: Apply online through the Berea admissions portal at no cost and file the 2027-2028 FAFSA; confirm the financial eligibility guidelines before applying.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to domestic and international applicants. Berea admits about 40 or fewer new international students per year and it is rare that more than one student from any country is offered admission in a year.
official.international_eligibility: Yes. Berea states all admitted international students receive financial aid and scholarships that cover 100% of tuition, housing, food, and fees; accepted international students pay a $2,200 enrollment deposit (adjustable for financial need) before the I-20 is issued, and participate in the Work Program without needing work permits.
official.duration: Four years (bachelor's degree), funded for all four years while the student remains enrolled and files the FAFSA annually
official.description: Berea College, the oldest continuously tuition-free college in the United States, awards the Tuition Promise Scholarship to every admitted student so no student pays tuition from personal income, and from Fall 2027 guarantees 100% of tuition, housing, food, fees and supplies without loans for all students.
official.program_type: Need-aware tuition promise awarded to all admitted students, not a competitive merit scholarship
official.english_requirement: Domestic applicants are test-optional (ACT code 1492 / SAT code 1060). International applicants must submit one of: TOEFL iBT 68 (paper-based 520), IELTS 6.0 overall with at least 5 in each subsection, Duolingo 95, SAT 980 combined, or ACT 19 composite, less than two years old; there is no test-optional route for international applicants. The Nursing major requires TOEFL iBT 83 with 26 on the spoken section.

applicant_utility.summary: Every admitted student receives the Tuition Promise, so the real challenge is passing Berea's financial eligibility screen and the admissions bar rather than winning an award. Check your household's adjusted gross income against Berea's published bands before applying (a two-parent family of four is 'highly likely' eligible under about $56,000), and file the 2027-2028 FAFSA early because it is required for admission itself. Domestic first-years should target the November 1 Early Action I date, while international applicants face one November 30 deadline, roughly 40 seats worldwide, and a $2,200 deposit after admission.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving students from families with limited financial resources who want a no-loan bachelor's degree and accept Berea's mandatory work program and financial-eligibility gate.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your family's adjusted gross income sits inside Berea's 'highly likely' or 'somewhat likely' band for your household size before investing time in the application
File the 2027-2028 FAFSA (Berea code 001955) as soon as it opens on October 1 - admission consideration requires it
Request final secondary records early; international transcripts must be certified English translations from school officials
Domestic applicants: decide test-optional versus submitting ACT/SAT scores (school codes ACT 1492, SAT 1060)
International applicants: book TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo early - scores must be under two years old, there is no test-optional route, and nursing aspirants need TOEFL iBT 83 with 26 speaking
Track the portal checklist to completion; Berea states incomplete applications will not be considered
common_rejection_risks: Missing FAFSA - it is required for admission, not merely for aid
Household income above the published financial-eligibility bands, which makes admission very unlikely regardless of grades
Submitting an incomplete application file; Berea does not review incomplete applications
International applicants relying on an English test score older than two years or assuming test-optional status applies
Missing the November 30 international deadline - Berea does not grant extensions
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Personal and indirect expenses (books, transportation and personal spending, estimated at about $3,900 per year on the 2026-27 cost of attendance) plus the $2,200 enrollment deposit for international students; from Fall 2027 the College states tuition, housing, food, fees and supplies are fully covered without loans.
document_audit: FAFSA must be refiled every year of enrollment - a missed refiling jeopardizes aid
International academic records need certified English translations by school officials
The Financial Resource Recommendation Form may not be completed by a close relative
The international personal essay (2-5 pages) must be entirely your own unassisted writing and is also used for course placement
Berea does not accept the CSS Profile or ISFSAA in place of its International Financial Questionnaire
alerts: The financial eligibility requirement is an admissions gate, not a scholarship criterion - failing it ends the application regardless of academics
International admission is extremely competitive: rarely more than one student per country is admitted in a given year
The full-funding guarantee (housing, food, fees, supplies) starts with the Fall 2027 entering class - students entering earlier pay housing, food and fees
No deadline extensions are granted, including for international applicants
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create an account on the Berea admissions portal, complete the application, upload documents and file the 2027-2028 FAFSA, then monitor the portal checklist until it shows complete.

Award notification March 2027. Dates for the next cycle are not yet published; the programme reopens annually each August.
official.application_cycle: 2027-28 cycle (closed); annual cycle reopens each August
official.status_note: AAUW states: 'Applications have closed for the 2027-28 academic year.' Award notifications for that cycle are issued in March 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Fellowship funds may be used for expenses incurred during the fellowship term, including educational costs such as tuition, fees, and required course materials (e.g., books and supplies), as well as living expenses, including housing, food, and dependent care (e.g., childcare).
official.funding_period: per fellowship term, paid in two equal instalments
benefits: International Fellowships carry a stipend of $20,000 for a master's degree and $25,000 for a doctorate degree
Stipends are payable to fellows only and are disbursed in two equal payments at the beginning and the midpoint of the fellowship term
Funds may be used for educational costs (tuition, fees, required course materials such as books and supplies) and living expenses (housing, food, and dependent care such as childcare)
eligibility: Applicants must identify as a woman
Applicants must be admitted or enrolled in their first master's or an academic or professional doctorate degree at the time of application, and the degree must be in one of the STEM disciplines
Applicants must begin their program on or before September 15, 2027, and complete it on or after April 30, 2028
Applicants must possess at least one academic degree (earned in the U.S. or abroad) that is equivalent to a U.S. bachelor's degree
Applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale for the highest degree earned, and may apply for only one degree type and in a single specific field

Applicants must pursue their study in the U.S. on a full-time basis at an institution accredited by the U.S. Department of Education, and must reside in the U.S. or country of their study for the duration of the fellowship period
Fellowship recipients must be non-U.S. citizens and must not hold U.S. permanent resident status, nor be applicants for U.S. permanent residency (green card)

Study outside the country of citizenship and the U.S. is considered only for citizens of travel-banned countries unable to secure a U.S. student visa, or for members of Graduate Women International who plan to study outside the United States

Not eligible: current AAUW Board members, AAUW employees, current AAUW Review Panelists and their immediate families, and previous AAUW fellowship or grant recipients (excluding Community Action Grants or branch/local AAUW awards)
requirements: Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale for the highest degree earned, with official proof
Full-time study in the U.S. at an institution accredited by the U.S. Department of Education (or approved study outside the U.S. under the stated conditions)
Program start on or before September 15, 2027 and completion on or after April 30, 2028; no exceptions are accommodated
Proof of English proficiency or an approved exemption, and proof of admission or current enrollment in the qualifying program
documents: Narrative application submitted through the AAUW Fellowships & Grants Application Portal

Two letters of recommendation from advisors, professors, colleagues or others academically or professionally familiar with the applicant; professional email addresses required; dossier services such as Interfolio or Parment are not accepted
Proof of degree: copies of all diplomas/degree certificates (or official transcripts showing conferral), with certified English translations for the highest earned degree
Official transcripts confirming conferral of all degrees received, including transfer-course grades where applicable
Copy of the cumulative grade point average (CGPA) calculation on a 4.0 scale showing at least 3.5, or a credential evaluation report from a service such as WES or ECE, or a Scholaro GPA conversion

Proof of English proficiency: TOEFL iBT 79, TOEFL Essentials 8.5, Revised TOEFL Paper-Delivered 60, IELTS 6.5, Cambridge Assessment 176, or Duolingo English Test 120; or a written statement affirming English is the applicant's native language; or a secondary diploma/undergraduate degree from an English-speaking institution, or one semester of full-time study in the discipline at an English-speaking institution
Proof of admission (official admission letter with anticipated start date, or deferral approval for 2027-28) or proof of enrollment (transcripts/course listings or enrollment verification letter)
Proof of Graduate Women International membership, required only for applicants not subject to a U.S. travel ban who plan to study outside the United States
Certified English translations for highest-earned-degree materials, and an explanation (e.g., marriage certificate) if the name on documents differs from the application
selection_criteria: Master's track: demonstrated academic and/or scholarly excellence; feasibility of the proposed academic, professional, or research plan; demonstrated commitment to women and girls; long-term career objectives and commitment to impact; strength and feasibility of the financial plan

Doctoral track: demonstrated academic and/or scholarly excellence; originality and potential contribution of the proposed work; feasibility of the proposed academic or research plan; demonstrated commitment to women and girls; long-term career objectives and commitment to impact; strength and feasibility of the financial plan

Preferential criteria when applicants demonstrate comparable merit: country with historically low representation among AAUW recipients, first international academic experience, residing in the home country at application, first-generation college graduate, raised in or leading a single-parent household, caregiving responsibilities, and institutional context (R2 institutions or institutions with limited research resources)
Only complete applications meeting all eligibility criteria are reviewed; recommendations are made by independent panels of scholars and STEM experts and are subject to final AAUW approval
coverage: Cash stipend of $20,000 (master's) or $25,000 (doctorate), payable to the fellow only, disbursed in two equal payments at the beginning and midpoint of the fellowship term
Eligible expenses: tuition, fees, required course materials (books and supplies), housing, food, and dependent care (childcare)
application_method: Visit the AAUW Fellowships & Grants Application Portal to create an account or log in and begin the narrative application
Register two recommenders as early as possible so each receives a personalized submission link; the application is not complete until recommendations are submitted
Upload all required documents and submit before the deadline; AAUW encourages starting well in advance of the close
official.application_route: Apply online through the AAUW Fellowships & Grants Application Portal with a narrative application, two recommendation letters and uploaded credential documents.
official.citizenship_residency: Recipients must be non-U.S. citizens, must not hold U.S. permanent resident status, and must not be applicants for U.S. permanent residency; applicants must reside in the U.S. or country of their study for the fellowship period.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the fellowship is specifically designed for women who are non-U.S. citizens or permanent residents.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The degree must be formally classified as STEM, determined by the DHS STEM Designated Degree Program List; eligibility follows the classification of the degree program, not the applicant's research topic. Professional doctorates (e.g., MD, PharmD, DVM) are included.
official.research_requirement: Master's applicants are not expected to present a formal research proposal unless research is part of their degree program; doctoral applicants must articulate a research interest, clinical focus or applied-practice project addressing an important question or gap, with emerging originality.
official.duration: One academic year (fellowship term); for the 2027-28 cycle fellows begin by September 15, 2027, the final report is due July 31, 2028, and the mid-year report is due December 2027.
official.description: AAUW's International Fellowships have supported international women pursuing full-time postgraduate study in the United States since 1917, awarding stipends of $20,000 for a master's degree or $25,000 for a doctorate to women in STEM who intend to apply their expertise, professional skills and leadership in service of their home countries.
official.program_type: Graduate fellowship (stipend) for international women pursuing STEM degrees
official.english_requirement: One of: TOEFL iBT 79, TOEFL Essentials 8.5, Revised TOEFL Paper-Delivered Test 60, IELTS 6.5, Cambridge Assessment 176, or Duolingo English Test 120 (institutional TOEFL scores are not accepted; scores are valid for two years except Cambridge, valid for life). Exemptions: a written statement affirming the applicant's native language is English, or a secondary diploma/undergraduate degree from an English-speaking institution, or one semester of full-time study in the applicant's discipline at an English-speaking institution.

applicant_utility.summary: This competitive stipend suits non-U.S. women with at least a bachelor's-equivalent degree and a 3.5/4.0 GPA who are admitted or enrolled in a full-time STEM master's or doctorate in the United States - you need the admission in hand before the September window opens, so sequence university applications first. Budget carefully: $20,000-$25,000 for the year arrives in two instalments with 14-30% U.S. tax withheld, so treat it as a substantial supplement rather than full coverage of graduate costs.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-U.S.-citizen women with strong academic records and a demonstrable record of empowering women and girls, holding or about to hold a place on a full-time STEM graduate programme in the U.S.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure admission or enrollment proof first - the application requires an admission letter with the anticipated start date (or a 2027-28 deferral approval), or an enrollment verification letter
Confirm the degree programme appears on the DHS STEM Designated Degree Program List, since eligibility follows the programme classification rather than your research topic
Verify your CGPA converts to at least 3.5 on a 4.0 scale and obtain official documentation (or a WES/ECE evaluation or Scholaro conversion) proving it
Register both recommenders in the portal early using professional email addresses - the file stays incomplete until recommendations land
Sit an accepted English test early (TOEFL iBT 79, IELTS 6.5, DET 120, Cambridge 176 or TOEFL Essentials 8.5); institutional TOEFL scores are rejected
Order certified English translations for highest-degree documents and collect transcripts for every degree before the window opens
common_rejection_risks: Programme starting after September 15, 2027 or completing before April 30, 2028 - no exceptions are accommodated
Cumulative GPA below 3.5 on a 4.0 scale for the highest degree earned
Holding or applying for U.S. permanent residency, or having previously received an AAUW fellowship or grant (other than Community Action Grants or branch/local awards)
Incomplete files - missing recommendations, untranslated credentials, institutional TOEFL scores or filler form-letter recommendations
Changing institution, field or programme type after the award recommendation, which is an automatic disqualification
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The stipend is the only award: U.S. graduate tuition and living costs commonly exceed $20,000-$25,000, and fellows cover their own visa fees, English test fees, credential evaluations and translations; stipends are subject to 14% or 30% U.S. tax withholding.
document_audit: Official transcripts must cover every degree received, including transfer courses with grades
The highest earned degree requires a certified translation if it was not issued in English
Dossier services (Interfolio, Parment) are not accepted and standardized or form-letter recommendations are discouraged
If your name differs across documents, an explanation such as a marriage certificate or court name-change letter is required
Graduate Women International membership proof is required only for non-travel-ban applicants planning to study outside the United States
alerts: The application window is roughly one month (mid-August to mid-September, closing 5:00pm ET) with no extensions - have every credential ready before it opens
Applying for a green card disqualifies recipients, and current U.S. permanent residents are ineligible
Money arrives in two instalments (first July-September 2027, second December 2027/January 2028), so early costs such as the enrollment deposit must be bridged
Mid-year (December 2027) and final (July 31, 2028) reports are binding fellowship obligations
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create an AAUW portal account, register two recommenders, complete the narrative application and upload credentials, then track the file until both recommendations are submitted before the cycle deadline.
